# Introduction

The **`ihcheterogeneity`** analysis (IHC Heterogeneity Analysis) provides clinicopathological researchers and biostatisticians with intuitive, publication-ready tools in jamovi and R.

## Key Capabilities

- With a reference measurement (whole section, hotspot or overall score): the Spearman
  correlation of each region with the reference, the absolute-agreement ICC(2,1), the per-case
  coefficient of variation, and for each region the mean difference from the reference with its
  95% CI and Bland-Altman limits of agreement.
- Without a reference: the same statistics between the regions.
- Each systematic difference is judged against a margin you set (`bias_margin`, default 5% of the
  comparison mean): ruled out when its 90% CI lies inside the margin (two one-sided tests), shown
  to be material when a Bonferroni-adjusted CI lies entirely beyond it, inconclusive otherwise.
- Optional variance components, sample-size planning for ICC precision (Bonett 2002) and
  comparisons between spatial compartments.

# Example Workflow in R

```r
library(ClinicoPath)

data("ihcheterogeneity_test", package = "ClinicoPath")

ihcheterogeneity(
  data = ihcheterogeneity_test,
  wholesection = "wholesection",
  biopsy1 = "biopsy1",
  biopsy2 = "biopsy2",
  biopsy3 = "biopsy3",
  biopsy4 = "biopsy4",
  spatial_id = "spatial_id",
  bias_margin = 5,
  compareCompartments = TRUE,
  showReportSentences = TRUE
)
```

# Clinical & Statistical Interpretation

The Clinical Assessment gives one verdict: agreement thresholds met (every systematic difference
ruled out within the margin), met but not confirmed, moderate, inadequate, not adequate for
substitution (a material systematic difference), or insufficient data. Choose the correlation
threshold, the CV threshold and the margin before looking at the results. The results describe
the cases analysed; they are not an external validation.
